content:
Aisha Bello: first week of provision-to-ready alerts is… loud 😅. seeing pages even when it’s just validation flakes that self-heal.

Aisha Bello: dashboards for context:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/provision-to-ready/overview?var-region=us-east&var-gpu=A100
- Alert list: https://grafana.redwood.ai/alerting/list?search=provision_to_ready

Aisha Bello: current paging rules:
- P95 time-to-ready > 45m for 15m (page)
- success rate < 97% over 30m (page)
- quarantine_count > 5 (page)

Aisha Bello: data from last 7 days (us-east/A100 only):
- P50 ~ 18–22m, P95 ranges 38–62m depending on day
- success rate generally 98–99.2%, but dips to 96.x% during NCCL smoke test flakes
- quarantine spikes correlate w/ the “driver parity” check when image channel flips candidate->stable

Aisha Bello: proposal: move most of this to ticketing while rollout is still gated. page only on sustained hard failures.

Miles Thornton: +1. right now the SLOs are aspirational; paging on P95 during week-1 makes oncall miserable.

Miles Thornton: reminder: what we *care* about paging on is “operators need to take action to restore capacity / stop customer impact”. P95 drift alone doesn’t always mean that.

Rafael Mendes: agree. I’m seeing pages where it resolves by itself in <10m. if we page, we need high confidence it’s not transient.

Rafael Mendes: also: oncall coverage this week is thinner (release train + other migrations). would prefer paging only for “pipeline is broken” scenarios.

Sergio Costa: what’s the biggest noisy alert right now? P95 or success rate?

Aisha Bello: success rate alert is the worst offender. it’s counting failures in validation steps (mostly NCCL timeout) even when retry succeeds on attempt 2.

Aisha Bello: we’re using `provision_to_ready_validation_result{result="fail"}` over 30m / total attempts. so retries inflate “failures”.

Allison Grant: yep, that metric is attempt-level. for alerting we should be using node-level terminal outcome.

Allison Grant: do we have `readiness_transition_total{to_state="Ready"}` vs `to_state="Quarantined"` / `to_state="Error"` (or equivalent) yet? that would be less noisy.

Aisha Bello: we have `fleet_readiness_state_transition_total` in the new pack (from PR-18441 + SLI calc PR). it’s a little delayed but good enough.

Sergio Costa: ok, we can rewrite success rate as:
`Ready / (Ready + Quarantined + Failed)` over a longer window, and only page if it’s REALLY bad.

Miles Thornton: for gating: we should page if we’re quarantining lots of nodes (capacity shortfall risk) OR time-to-ready is catastrophically bad.

Rafael Mendes: + also page if the readiness service is not writing states (control plane outage), since that blocks bring-up entirely.

Aisha Bello: draft new policy:

1) Paging (sev2 page):
- "Provision-to-ready hard failure": `fleet_readiness_state_transition_total{to_state=~"Quarantined|Failed"}` / total transitions > 10% for 60m AND count >= 20 nodes
- "Readiness pipeline stalled": no `to_state="Ready"` transitions for 30m while `Allocated` transitions are happening (i.e. we’re allocating but not progressing)
- "Time-to-ready catastrophic": P95 > 90m for 60m (only if node volume >= 20)

2) Ticket (non-page):
- P95 > 60m for 2h
- Quarantine count > 5 (but no page), with breakdown by top failure reason
- Validation flake rate (attempt-level) > 5% for 2h

Aisha Bello: plus: add a "paging suppression" during feature-flag ramp (first 24h in a region) unless success rate < 85%.

Sergio Costa: suppression can be done via alert labels + routing in Alertmanager (route by `rollout_phase=canary`). Do we have that label on metrics?

Allison Grant: we can label off region + pool_type, but rollout_phase isn’t in metrics today. easier: annotate in Grafana and keep paging thresholds conservative.

Miles Thornton: I’d avoid too much dynamic suppression logic. keep it simple.

Sean Gallagher: catching up. I’m aligned with this direction. paging should be reserved for “humans needed now”. ticket for tuning/flake work.

Sean Gallagher: two asks:
1) ensure we have explicit ownership in the alert description (Infra vs Platform vs SRE)
2) ensure paging alerts link directly to dashboard + runbook section (triage path)

Rafael Mendes: +1. also: please set the paging alerts to page *one* rotation (eng-sre) and create a ticket for infra automatically (don’t fanout page infra).

Aisha Bello: ok. I’ll update the rules to:
- page `eng-sre` only
- add `owner_team` label in alert rule (likely `owner_team="infra-fleet"` but page stays with SRE)
- include runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENGINFRA/Provision-to-ready+failures+triage+runbook

Sergio Costa: I can take the actual rule updates in observability-pack PR. drop me the exact PromQL you want.

Aisha Bello: PromQL sketches:

- terminal failure ratio:
`sum(rate(fleet_readiness_state_transition_total{to_state=~"Quarantined|Failed",region="us-east"}[60m]))
 /
 sum(rate(fleet_readiness_state_transition_total{to_state=~"Ready|Quarantined|Failed",region="us-east"}[60m]))`

- stalled pipeline:
`sum(rate(fleet_readiness_state_transition_total{to_state="Ready"}[30m])) == 0
 and
 sum(rate(fleet_readiness_state_transition_total{to_state="Allocated"}[30m])) > 0`

- P95 catastrophic (if we have histogram):
`histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(provision_to_ready_seconds_bucket[60m])) by (le)) > 5400`

Allison Grant: make sure the histogram query is grouped by (region,gpu_type,pool_type) not globally. global P95 is misleading.

Aisha Bello: yup. for paging we’ll scope to region+gpu_type where rollout is active (right now us-east/A100).

Miles Thornton: also add minimum sample size guard. otherwise 1 weird node can page.

Sergio Costa: we can do `and sum(increase(fleet_readiness_state_transition_total{to_state=~"Ready|Quarantined|Failed"}[60m])) >= 20`.

Rafael Mendes: great.

Sean Gallagher: decision from SRE side:
- ship the new paging thresholds this week
- keep P95>60m as ticket-only until we exit canary
- re-evaluate after another 7 days, especially once NCCL timeout fixes land

Aisha Bello: ack. I’ll open a follow-up in Linear for “alerting v2 after canary” + note that attempt-level validation fail metric isn’t suitable for paging.

Sergio Costa: I’ll push the PR today and tag @Aisha @Allison for review.

Allison Grant: thanks. pls include description text explicitly stating “attempt-level metrics are for debugging; terminal transitions are authoritative”.

Aisha Bello: will do. :thumbsup:

Rafael Mendes: once merged, can we schedule it to go live during business hours? want to avoid surprise route changes overnight.

Sergio Costa: yep, I’ll merge before 5pm PT and we can watch for 30m.

Sean Gallagher: perfect. keep me posted if paging noise continues after the change.
